intended_object: For a finite family F of compact opens of X, the stage is the set of realized membership patterns, a subspace of the Sierpiński product Prop^F. For U ∈ F, coordinateOpen is the open set {v | U ∈ v}, i.e. the preimage of the open point of Sierpiński space under the U-th coordinate projection. This comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The carrier is {v | v.1 U}: the patterns whose U-coordinate holds. It is open because the U-th projection, composed with the subtype inclusion, is continuous into Prop, and a set given by a continuous Prop-valued predicate is open (`continuous_Prop`). This is exactly the standard subbasic cylinder open in a subspace of a product of Sierpiński spaces. The library checks that its preimage under `point` is U itself (`point_preimage_coordinateOpen`), which confirms the intended meaning. The definition makes no extra assumptions: X is an arbitrary topological space and F an arbitrary finite family. Mathlib has no ready-made notion of this library-specific stage, so there is no counterpart. The definition is correct and stated at its natural generality.
